metadata.title: Fifteen Of Sixteen
metadata.continues_from: zero-for-sixteen/ (Mycroft6, last built entry in the series) -- this reel's cold open directly answers that video's closing measurement (zero of thirty-one real conflicts) with the fix that killed fifteen of the sixteen false positives, and per the script's own header assumes Mycroft6's recap chapter is common knowledge rather than re-teaching it.
metadata.build_note: 2026-09-20: initial authoring pass, not a rebuild. 18 beats (B00-B17), one more than Mycroft6's 16, matching this script's own PRODUCTION NOTES table of 16 named figures (one more than Mycroft6's 12) plus Chapter 5's own two-list split (same convention as Mycroft6's B12/B13) plus a no-dedicated-figure 'true now' beat mirroring that same precedent. Unlike Mycroft6, this script's own runtime estimate is accurate: counted 1,343 words directly against the script's own claimed 1,343 -- exact match -- so no runtime-cut pass was needed; narration_text is close to verbatim with only light TTS normalization (numbers spelled out, em dashes to commas) and one small rephrase in B00 to avoid a repeated 'that's not X, that's Y' construction the script's own cold open used twice in a row.

approvals.notes: Added retroactively per fellows/divij-pawar/CLAUDE.md SS4 (PIPELINE-SAFETY.md) voice/notes approval gate -- this build's audio was already generated before this gate was written into house doctrine. Left as PENDING, not backfilled as approved: a human still needs to run ./art approvals --fingerprints and sign off for real before this reel's re-render is treated as gate-clean.

beats.narration_text: Last video ended on a number. Zero for sixteen. Zero real conflicts, out of sixteen flagged runs. This video, the fix landed. Fifteen of those sixteen false positives, gone. But the test built to prove that fix actually works found something else instead. Two agents were given the exact same data. One of them didn't read it. It invented a different quarter for a filing that doesn't exist. It cited a source URL nobody gave it. This is a model that doesn't do the reading, not a comparator bug.

props.command: What did the fix that killed fifteen false positives actually find?
output: Fifteen of sixteen false positives, killed the day they measured it
The test built to prove it works found a different problem instead
One agent invented a quarter, a filing, and a source URL, all fake

shot.concept: COLD OPEN LAW, per house convention confirmed against zero-for-sixteen (Mycroft6): B00 is fixed as the Remotion bookend and carries the cold open's VO plus the TITLE CARD info (topic/segment), rather than a custom Manim animation. Figure 1 ('sixteen-to-fifteen', the script's own cold-open card) is deferred to B16's close reprise, where it lands with full payoff weight as the OUTRO-LAW dense-callout beat -- same pattern as Mycroft6's fig1. Figure 2 ('fabricated-quarter', the real-vs-invented context comparison) is referenced in the narration here but its full visual treatment is deferred to B08, which renders the same real-vs-fabricated imagery with more room. REPHRASED (not a cut, a register fix): the script's own cold open ends on two consecutive 'That's not X. That's Y.' sentences back to back; this build merged them into one sentence ('This is a model that doesn't do the reading, not a comparator bug') to avoid the repeated construction reading as a stock rhetorical tic, without changing the claim.

beats.act: chapter 1 - the two threads left open
beats.narration_text: Quick recap, for anyone new. Sixteen of thirty-one real runs this tool ever produced were false positives. Two agents were flagged as disagreeing when they'd simply been asked about different things. Zero were real conflicts. The diagnosis named two ways forward. Link each number to the concept it came from. Then the comparator stops comparing apples to someone else's oranges. Or actually test whether two agents can ever be shown the same fact. Nothing in thirty-one runs had put them in that position. One day. Both threads. In that order.

shot.concept: Figure 3 (open-threads). Two paths branching from last week's closing card: LINK CONCEPTS and TEST OVERLAP, with the recap number (16/31, 0 real conflicts) stated first per the script's own 'quick recap for anyone new' framing.

show.event: title: 'WHAT LAST WEEK LEFT UNRESOLVED'
recap chip: '16 / 31 FALSE POSITIVES -- 0 REAL CONFLICTS'
a card labeled 'LAST WEEK' branches into two paths: 'LINK CONCEPTS' / 'TEST OVERLAP'
caption: 'one day, both threads, in that order'
hold

beats.narration_text: The idea is simple to say. Every number a producer cites gets tagged with the concept it came from: Assets, Revenue, Diluted Earnings Per Share. If a number's concept could never plausibly come from the other producer, its absence there stops counting as a disagreement. The two producers' concept lists don't overlap at all, by design. So a tagged number is excluded from comparison entirely. Only the untagged ones, bare ratios with no label nearby, still get compared the old way.

shot.concept: Figure 4 (number-tagging). A conclusion sentence with each number getting a colored concept tag: Assets, Revenue, and one number left grey (untagged) -- confirmed directly: validation/concept_linkage.py's docstring names Assets/Revenues/NetIncomeLoss vs EarningsPerShareDiluted as the two disjoint concept sets.

show.event: title: 'TAG THE NUMBER, NOT JUST THE DIGITS'
a conclusion sentence renders with its numbers highlighted
colored tags drop onto two numbers: 'ASSETS', 'REVENUE'; one number stays grey, untagged
chip: 'TAGGED NUMBERS -- EXCLUDED FROM COMPARISON ENTIRELY'
hold

beats.narration_text: Three bugs surfaced before the numbers could be trusted. A decimal point inside a figure was mistaken for the end of a sentence. That hid a concept label sitting earlier in the same real sentence. The tagger only recognized natural-language phrasing, like "diluted EPS." It missed that the actual prompt format is the raw label itself, "EarningsPerShareDiluted," which models echo back verbatim. And distance to a label was measured from its start, not its end. That mis-matched two numbers named together in one sentence, with the closest label winning for the wrong one. All three were caught by tests before the measurement was trusted.

shot.concept: Figure 5 (three-bugs). Three bug cards, each struck through FIXED with a one-line cause -- all three independently confirmed directly against validation/concept_linkage.py: the decimal/sentence-boundary split, the verbatim EarningsPerShareDiluted echo the tagger missed, and the label-distance-measured-from-start bug.

show.event: title: 'THREE BUGS, CAUGHT BEFORE TRUST'
bug card 1: 'decimal point mistaken for end of sentence'
bug card 2: 'tagger missed the raw echo: EarningsPerShareDiluted'
bug card 3: 'distance measured from label start, not end'
all three cards strike through, stamped 'FIXED'
hold

beats.narration_text: Then the actual test. Not a new example built to prove the point. The sixteen real runs already sitting in last week's labeled record, the ones already flagged as false positives. Replay all sixteen through the new rule. Count what's left.

shot.concept: Figure 6 (replay-through-gate). The sixteen labeled record tiles from Mycroft6 filing one at a time through a gate labeled concept_aware -- confirmed directly: tests/fixtures/cross_agent_real_runs_corpus.json has exactly 16 entries labeled disjoint_concepts, and tests/test_concept_linkage.py replays them.

show.event: chip: 'NOT A NEW EXAMPLE -- THE SAME 16 REAL RUNS'
16 small tiles fade in in a row
tiles file one at a time through a gate labeled 'concept_aware'
caption: 'replay all sixteen, count what's left'
hold

beats.narration_text: Fifteen stop flagging. The sixteenth doesn't. That's the one where a number really was fabricated. It's supposed to still flag. Zero new false positives anywhere else in the corpus. Checked twice, not once. Once against the tagging logic by itself. Then again through the exact function the live comparison route actually calls. That confirms the wiring didn't quietly change the answer.

shot.concept: Figure 7 (checked-twice). Two check panels, MODULE, DIRECT: 15/16 and PRODUCTION API: 15/16, landing on the same number -- confirmed directly: tests/test_concept_linkage.py::TestConceptAwareFlagAgainstCorpus tests the module directly, tests/test_real_run_corpus.py::TestConceptAwareRuleAgainstCorpus tests the production function, exactly the double-check the script describes.

show.event: '15 STOP FLAGGING' resolves, large
'the sixteenth doesn't' -- a small stamp: 'REALLY FABRICATED. SUPPOSED TO STILL FLAG.'
two panels draw in: 'MODULE, DIRECT: 15/16' and 'PRODUCTION API: 15/16'
both panels land on the same number, connecting line between them
hold

beats.narration_text: Fifteen of sixteen real false positives, killed. The one survivor is the one confirmed real catch on record. It's the one fabricated number this tool has ever actually caught.

shot.concept: Figure 8 (true-positive-preserved). The 15/1 card relabeled, deliberately short (11s) since it's this chapter's summary beat, per the same 'shortest of the chapter, recaps rather than introduces' convention used in Mycroft5/Mycroft6.

show.event: '15 KILLED' / '1' card fades in
stamp lands on the '1': 'TRUE POSITIVE, PRESERVED'
caption: 'the one confirmed real catch on record'
hold

beats.narration_text: Here's the test nothing in thirty-one runs had ever performed. Give both agents the exact same evidence. Not two different lenses on one company. The identical numbers. Then see if a real disagreement can even happen. Two local models. Same prompt, same data, same directive. Four runs. Apple twice, with the models swapped between roles to rule out a role effect. Then Microsoft. Then Nvidia.

shot.concept: Figure 9 (shared-context-fork). One shared context block forking into two model icons, qwen2.5:7b and mistral-7b -- confirmed directly: RUN_LOG's 2026-09-11 entry names both models pulled locally via Ollama, and the roles-swapped AAPL control run.

show.event: chip: 'SAME DATA. TWO MODELS.'
one context block draws in, then forks into two model icons: 'qwen2.5:7b' / 'mistral-7b'
four run labels tick in: 'AAPL' / 'AAPL (roles swapped)' / 'MSFT' / 'NVDA'
caption: 'a role effect, ruled out'
hold

beats.narration_text: Four for four, flagged. The first time this flag has ever fired on evidence both sides actually saw. But not because the two models disagreed about a number. In three of the four runs, one model cited zero of the real figures. It invented a fiscal quarter that isn't in the data. It cited a source URL nobody gave it.

shot.concept: Figure 10 (zero-real-numbers), plus B00's deferred figure 2 payoff -- the real-vs-fabricated context comparison rendered in full here, with more room than the cold open had. Confirmed directly: RUN_LOG names 3 of 4 runs as mistral-7b failing to use the real context, inventing a fiscal quarter and a source URL.

show.event: '4 FOR 4, FLAGGED' resolves, large
caption: 'first time on evidence both sides actually saw'
real Apple context renders on the left; on the right, the fabricated quarter and a struck-through fake URL
red stamp: '0 REAL NUMBERS CITED'
hold

beats.narration_text: In the fourth run, roles were swapped, so this isn't about which seat the model sat in. It did read the real numbers. It still turned a real one hundred one billion, four hundred sixty-four million dollars of net income into a "net income loss" of negative one hundred one million. Wrong sign. Wrong by a factor of a thousand.

shot.concept: Figure 11 (sign-and-magnitude). Real $101,464,000,000 net income against the mislabeled '-$101,000,000 net income loss' -- confirmed directly: RUN_LOG's 4th-run result names this exact wrong-sign, thousand-times magnitude error for the roles-swapped run.

show.event: chip: 'ROLES SWAPPED -- NOT A SEAT EFFECT'
real figure resolves: '$101,464,000,000 net income'
an arrow points to the wrong output: '-$101,000,000 net income loss'
stamp: 'WRONG SIGN. WRONG BY 1000x.'
hold

beats.narration_text: The other model got every real figure right, all four times. It just wasn't clean either. It also added a return-on-equity number that appears nowhere in what it was given. So the mechanism works. It found a real problem. Just not the one it was built to find.

shot.concept: Figure 12 (model-scoreboard), plus the chapter's closing line. Split scoreboard: model A (qwen2.5:7b) 4/4 correct figures + 1 unsupported ROE added; model B (mistral-7b) 0/4 grounded -- confirmed directly against RUN_LOG's result section.

show.event: scoreboard draws: 'MODEL A -- 4/4 CORRECT, +1 UNSUPPORTED ROE'
second row: 'MODEL B -- 0/4 GROUNDED'
caption: 'the mechanism works. it found a real problem.'
caption: 'just not the one it was built to find'
hold

beats.narration_text: A second session, same day, turned the measurement into a decision: ship it. The live comparison route now runs the concept-aware check by default, not the old rule. Two things came along for free.

shot.concept: Figure 13 (route-rewire). The /api/compare route diagram, old rule struck through, concept_aware wired in by default -- confirmed directly against RUN_LOG's second 2026-09-11 entry and web/server.py.

show.event: title: 'WIRING THE FIX IN -- SAME DAY'
'/api/compare' route diagram draws
the old rule strikes through
'concept_aware' wires in, labeled 'DEFAULT NOW'
hold

beats.narration_text: First, the old rule had its own quiet failure. It required both agents to cite at least one number before flagging anything. That's what suppressed the one confirmed true positive in the first place. The new rule never had that requirement. Switching to it fixed a second, separate bug, with no extra code. Second: a real extraction bug, found while building last week's corpus. A large number with commas and no dollar sign was getting truncated to its last three digits. Thirteen billion, nine hundred seventy-one million dollars was extracting as the string zero-zero-zero point zero. It's fixed. It's confirmed against the real historical case, not just a new example built to pass.

shot.concept: Figure 14 (regex-fix), plus the old-rule's-quiet-failure finding. '13,971,000,000.0' crossing out '000.0', replaced with the corrected full string -- confirmed directly: core/numeric.py's own 2026-09-11 comment names this exact fix. The both-sides-non-empty gate removal is confirmed against the same RUN_LOG entry's Result section.

show.event: chip: 'FIX #1 -- THE OLD GATE'S QUIET FAILURE'
caption: 'required both sides non-empty -- suppressed the true positive'
stamp: 'NEW RULE: NO SUCH GATE'
chip: 'FIX #2 -- A REAL EXTRACTION BUG'
'13,971,000,000.0' renders, then crosses out down to '000.0'
the corrected full string resolves in green
hold

beats.narration_text: And the fabrication check that already existed for single-agent chats had never once been connected to this comparison route. It extracts every claim a model makes. It checks each one against its own cited source. It is now connected. Replayed against the exact historic fabrication, not a clean example. The citation supports none of the numbers under it. A real, automatic signal. Not "this number is fake." It's "this source doesn't back what's claimed here." That's what actually caught it.

shot.concept: Figure 15 (verification-rate-zero). The real 2026-08-29 thought log, citation highlighted, VERIFICATION RATE: 0.0 stamped beside it -- confirmed directly: this is the same historic fabrication case (0.34 debt-to-equity) SOURCES.md already verified for Mycroft6, now replayed through claim verification wired into web/server.py for the first time.

show.event: title: 'CLAIM VERIFICATION, WIRED IN FOR THE FIRST TIME'
the real 2026-08-29 thought log renders, its citation highlighted
'VERIFICATION RATE: 0.0' stamps in beside it
chip: 'A REAL SIGNAL, NOT A GUESS'
hold

beats.act: chapter 5a - the honest ledger, true now
beats.narration_text: True now that wasn't a week ago. Fifteen of sixteen real false positives, gone. Measured against every run this tool has ever produced, not four. Sixteen. The one suppressed true positive fires again, as a side effect of the same fix. A comma-formatted number extracts correctly instead of losing everything but its last three digits. Claim verification runs on this comparison route for the first time. It produces a real signal against the one case that matters. Four ledger issues closed in one day. The comparison route has automated tests for the first time ever, three of them. Two hundred forty-two tests, up from two hundred twenty-four, green at every step.

shot.concept: No dedicated figure in the numbered table -- same convention as Mycroft6's B12: the script's own VISUAL direction is explicit, 'List one, building line by line.' Six checked() lines resolve one at a time, each a callback to a beat already shown earlier (B05/B06's 15/16, B12's suppression fix, B12's regex fix, B13's verification signal, B03's bug count, and the 242/224 test count).

show.event: title: 'TRUE NOW THAT WASN'T'
line 1: 'fifteen of sixteen false positives gone -- measured on all sixteen, not four'
line 2: 'the suppressed true positive fires again'
line 3: 'comma-formatted numbers extract correctly'
line 4: 'claim verification runs on this route for the first time'
line 5: 'four ledger issues closed in one day'
line 6: '242 tests, up from 224, green at every step'
hold on the full list

beats.act: chapter 5b - the honest ledger, still not true + uncommitted
beats.narration_text: Still not true. A legitimate ratio and a fabricated one still look identical to this system. Both are just numbers with no label nearby. Narrowing that gap from "any disconnected number" to "any unlabeled one" does not close it. Whatever's actually wrong with one of the two local models used in this test hasn't been investigated. Maybe it's reading its own input. Maybe it's a specific quantization. Maybe it's this prompt shape. It's flagged, not fixed. It's a different kind of problem than anything this tool was designed to catch. The comparison route has three tests now. Every other route, and every line of interface code, still has zero. The four critical security findings from the original audit are exactly as open as they were. And the pile of work sitting outside version control got bigger again. Eleven more files, on top of everything already sitting there uncommitted.

shot.concept: Figure 16 (uncommitted-growing), plus the script's own second Chapter-5 VISUAL direction ('List two, in warning color, held on screen. Do not clear it.'). This is the reel's longest and most protected beat by design -- the script's own production notes say 'never cut chapter 5, and never cut the still-not-true list inside it.' git log stays at the same commit as Mycroft6 (c53746a); the file counter ticks up again from 56 to a higher number, per the script's own framing of the pile 'getting bigger again.'

line 1: 'a real ratio and a fabricated one still look identical'
line 2: 'narrowed the gap, did not close it'
line 3: 'one local model's grounding failure -- flagged, not fixed'
line 4: 'comparison route: 3 tests. every other route and all interface code: 0'
line 5: '4 critical security findings -- exactly as open as before'
the full warning list holds, uncleared, as a git-log panel fades in beneath it: commit c53746a, unchanged
a file counter ticks up again: '+11 MORE FILES'

beats.narration_text: So here's the smallest true claim. The tool got better at not crying wolf. Fifteen fewer false alarms, for free, the same day they were measured. That's real. It did not get better at telling a real number from a convincing fake one. Those are different problems. A comparator that stops over-flagging is one thing. A comparator that catches fabrication is another. Zero-for-sixteen got solved for one reason, and stayed unsolved for the other. Mixing those two up is exactly the overclaim this format exists to catch. Fifteen of sixteen. One left. And one model that, this week, showed it can't be trusted to read its own homework.
